subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should the shared state DB policy be RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI access, a stricter single-writer gateway lease, or both for health/status/stability and doctor repair paths?
rationale: Current source confirms mutable CLI-side shared DB open and checkpoint paths, but the durable fix changes ownership between gateway RPC observability, plugin-state probes, doctor migrations, and operator recovery behavior.

options.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Make status, health, and stability ask the running gateway first, and make fallback file opens read-only with no journal or checkpoint pragmas while a gateway is active.

options.title: Single-writer gateway lease
options.body: Have the gateway own write and WAL-maintenance access to the shared state DB, with non-gateway processes failing closed or routing through gateway APIs unless they acquire an explicit maintenance lease.

options.title: Forensic harness first
options.body: Pause implementation until the reporter's sanitized DB bundle or a native runtime harness confirms the exact OpenClaw helper/runtime interaction.

recommendation.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Make status, health, and stability ask the running gateway first, and make fallback file opens read-only with no journal or checkpoint pragmas while a gateway is active.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across the DB-first runtime-state architecture and current gateway/CLI ownership boundaries traced to that work.
